title: Style: Lessons in Clarity and Grace, the chapter on clarity
author: Joseph M. Williams and Joseph Bizup
url: no address is stable for a printed book; the edition is named in `version`
version: 12th edition, 2017; the text was not fetched in this container

record.source: Metadiscourse is prose that talks about the writing rather than about its subject -- hedges and emphatics, attributors, narrators, and announcements or signposts such as "this section will show" -- and a short passage should hold little of it, because it costs the reader attention that the content does not repay.
record.kept: The category and its instruction: cut what points at the text instead of at the subject.
record.rewritten: Williams measures it as a proportion of the sentences; this repository tests a sentence by what the reader would lose, because a guard -- a boundary the reader would otherwise cross -- is metadiscourse that earns its place.
record.added: The ladder as the recurring arrangement: an announcement, a general claim, then a restatement of the claim, which a per-sentence test reads as three carriers.
record.dropped: The proportion guidance, and the hedge/emphatic/attributor/narrator taxonomy, which a writer cannot apply without counting.
